items.reason: IA carboplatin is given identically in both arms and is described as institutional standard ("it is nowadays considered a standard of care for relapsing tumours in our institution"). Rule 3 (C3) makes a drug that every arm receives soc_backbone; the question is Caelyx versus etoposide phosphate added to IA carboplatin. Carboplatin is not a D6 established GBM therapy, and IA catheter delivery is a route, not a device, so neither exception to rule 3 applies.

"IA carboplatin (400 mg/m^2)" is the same in both experimental arms and is the institution's standard IA agent ("carboplatin is the primary chemotherapeutic agent for IA infusions"), so it is backbone under C3.
With carboplatin as backbone, IA Caelyx (pegylated liposomal doxorubicin) is the only investigational agent in "IA Carboplatin + IA Caelyx", so rule 4 applies even on a backbone (C1).
IA etoposide phosphate is the only investigational agent in "IA Carboplatin + IA Etoposide Phosphate", the carboplatin being backbone.

The record calls carboplatin "At the heart of the present study", but the randomised comparison is between the two add-on agents. The carboplatin dose, route and schedule are identical across arms, which is the C3 case.
The non-candidate antitumour partner in the experimental arms is IA carboplatin (soc_backbone). Doxorubicin and etoposide are the candidates themselves, in separate arms.

note: S6 is met either way. Only carboplatin's candidate status (an approved oncology drug) depends on the C3 reading. Both candidates are approved oncology drugs given intra-arterially (formulation_flag new_route; the etoposide prodrug/new_route difference is priority 3 and not adjudicated). 'Glioblastoma multiforme' makes the terminology historical.
